The CrFeNiSi0.2 MEA was produced by arc melting a mixture of metals (purity > 99.9 wt%) in a high-purity argon atmosphere. To ensure chemical uniformity, the resulting ingots underwent eight melting cycles.
Melted alloys were drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold to form 2 × 10 × 100 mm3 plates
which were subsequently homogenized at 1200 ◦C for 2 h (denoted as HT-1200)
Subsequently, plates were rolled to achieve a 70 % reduction in thickness at room temperature.

evidence.quote: 900 ◦C for 1 h followed by solution treatment at 1100 ◦C for 1 min (AS-1100). All thermo-mechanical treatments were conducted in air and concluded with water quenching.
it was confirmed that CrFeNiSi0.2 MEA exhibits both FCC and σ phases, thereby corroborating the experimental results.
After aging at 800 ◦C for 1 h, the size of the σ phase does not exceed 2 μ m, predominantly exhibiting an ellipsoidal shape.

attributes.location: predominantly at grain boundaries, minor presence within grains

evidence.quote: after aging at 900 ◦C for 1 h, the morphology of the σ phase transitions from the ellipsoidal shape observed at 800 ◦C to a lath-like shape, with the maximum length of the lath-like σ phase exceeding 5 μ m.
After aging at 900 ◦C for 24 hh, the size of the σ phase decreases to about 2 μ m
